key_insight: Large language models can speed up literature screening and parameter extraction for infectious disease modeling, with accuracy high enough to be useful when workflows are carefully designed.
clinical_relevance: For outbreak modelers, LLMs may reduce manual review time for extracting key COVID-19 transmission parameters, while still requiring human checks for provenance and misassigned values.
method: Built an open-source end-to-end pipeline to screen PubMed/medRxiv records and extract reproduction number, serial interval, and incubation period from full-text PDFs.
Tested four LLMs on 2,067 COVID-19-era records and compared performance with human screening and a 50-article extraction gold standard.
Pooled extracted values into an SEIR model and ran sensitivity analyses, including model ensembling, to assess trade-offs in recall and precision.
evidence_signal: Screening reached 0.72-0.95 sensitivity and 0.92-0.99 specificity; extraction F1 was 0.90-0.96 for sparse articles but recall dropped to 0.38-0.78 across dense articles.
watch_item: Incomplete extraction in dense papers was mainly driven by prompting and output formatting, and misassignment of values shows that human validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Using large language models to facilitate literature review and data extraction for infectious disease models: COVID-19 as a test case
